01 / Material study / 2025

Form Study 001.

Year
2025
Medium
Chrome / CGI
Role
Concept, model, render

A single ribbon of chrome, folded until it holds itself up. When does a shape stop reading as geometry and start reading as an object with weight?

Modelled as one continuous surface, left deliberately unstyled. All the weight comes from the light: a wide soft key, one cold rim to separate metal from wall, a long contact shadow.

Over eleven passes the fold moved less than a centimetre. The last change was four degrees of rotation, which stopped the loop looking symmetrical.

Passes
11
Render
8 min/frame
Surface
Brushed chrome

04 / Form & light study / 2023

In Between.

Year
2023
Medium
CGI / glass
Role
Study, render

A cobalt torus held just off the ground, close enough that the light passing through it lands on the floor and does most of the work.

The object is simple; the shadow is what the photograph is actually of. The height was tuned frame by frame until the ring of light broke into feathered highlights.

The last piece in a year of studying transparency — and the first where I let glass smudge instead of keeping it clean.

Height
40 mm off floor
Caustic
Multi-pass
Surface
Cobalt glass

03 / Digital sculpture / 2024

Quiet Rhythm.

Year
2024
Medium
CGI / limestone
Role
Sculpt, lighting

Seven discs of the same stone, stacked with small offsets until the column looks unstable but never falls.

The rhythm is in the spacing, not the shapes. Each disc is identical; what changes is how much lean you can accumulate before the stack reads as broken.

The stone uses a scanned limestone surface with specular pulled almost to zero — any shine made it read as painted foam.

Discs
7
Angle
12° lean
Surface
Limestone

02 / Silicone study / 2025

Soft Matter.

Year
2025
Medium
CGI / silicone
Role
Form, shading, stills

Rendering something that looks like it would give way under your thumb — and keeping it interesting without a single hard edge.

No straight lines, no visible seams, so the eye has nothing to hold except shading. Most of the work was subsurface scattering and one very large, very soft light.

It began as a set of nine. Only this one survived — the others looked like food, or like toys.

Variants
9
Light
1 softbox
Surface
Matte silicone
